name: Amy True
line: Politicised hip-hop with jazz and soul at its core.
bio: British-born poet and songwriter of Irish and Ugandan heritage. Since 2011 Amy True has made politicised hip-hop fused with jazz and soul: conscious, iconoclastic verse set against melodic hooks and rich jazz instrumentation.
highlights: Touring the UK and Europe since 2011
November 2026 tour: Bristol, Maribor, Vienna, Innsbruck, Salzburg, Bern, Basel

name: The Mouse Outfit
format: DJ set, soundsystem with MCs, or 8-piece band
line: Jazz-influenced boom bap, from soundsystem to eight-piece band.
bio: A hip-hop production collective and live band from Manchester, fronted by MCs Koj and Ayite. Shows scale from DJ sets and soundsystem nights with MCs to a full eight-piece live band, with special guests at selected dates. The sound is jazz-influenced boom bap.
highlights: Three independent studio albums, including Jagged Tooth Crook (2018)
Collaborations with more than 85 musicians and vocalists
More than 15 million YouTube views
UK tour in autumn 2026

name: Dargz
line: Hip-hop and soul-infused jazz with more than 120 million streams.
bio: New York-born, London-based alt-jazz producer making joyous, hip-hop and soul-infused jazz that mixes hazy nostalgia with inventive production. Debut album Happiness passed 120 million streams. Second album Friends & Family features Mercury Prize-nominated collaborators.
highlights: 120+ million streams on debut album Happiness
Collaborations with Moses Boyd and Joe Webb
Support from BBC 6 Music, Jazz FM, Clash, Wonderland and SZA

name: The Hempolics
line: Rootsy modern reggae with soundsystem bass.
bio: The Hempolics bring organic, rootsy elements back to contemporary reggae. Led by Grippa Laybourne, the band pairs radio-friendly melodies with soundsystem bass. Laybourne spent years recording internationally acclaimed artists before assembling the band to realise his own vision.
highlights: Single Serious reached number one on the UK reggae chart
Serious playlisted during Massive Attack's BBC Radio takeover
London headline show at 229, May 2026

name: Kolinga
line: French, English and Lingala vocals over groove and trance.
bio: A French ensemble led by vocalist Rébecca M'Boungou, singing in French, English and Lingala. Drawing on the roots of Black music, Kolinga balances emotional depth with groove, rhythm and trance.
highlights: Vocals in French, English and Lingala
Rébecca M'Boungou (vocals), Arnaud Estor (guitar), Jérôme Martineau-Ricotti (drums), Nico Martin (bass), Jérémie Poirier-Quinot (keys, flute), Vianney Desplantes (euphonium, flugabone)

name: Plantfood
line: Spiritual jazz meets club music, electronic and acoustic.
bio: A six-piece jazz ensemble from Leeds combining electronic and acoustic instruments. High-energy sets move from intricate compositions to immersive soundscapes, drawing on The Prodigy, John Coltrane and Nubiyan Twist.
highlights: Six-piece electronic and acoustic line-up

line: The debut project of Nubiyan Twist's Jonathan Enser.

name: Izo Fitzroy
format: Band with up to nine gospel backing vocalists
line: Honest songwriting, built for a live room and a gospel choir.
bio: A raw, dynamic performer with honest songwriting written for the stage. Sincere lyrics sit over tight, melodic grooves. Her band is unconventional for soul: up to nine gospel backing vocalists make for live shows people talk about.
highlights: Live line-up of up to nine gospel backing vocalists
Known for unusual vocal arrangements in a soul setting

name: Kongo Dia Ntotila
line: Congolese guitar, jazz and African dance music.
bio: KDN draw on rhythmic and sonic traditions from the motherland: beats, bass grooves and the euphoric sunshine of Congolese guitars. African dance music meets jazz, with polyrhythmic guitars, horns and vocals, which they call pure Afro-joy.
highlights: African dance music fused with jazz
Polyrhythmic guitars, horns and vocals

line: Accessible melodies and hypnotic rhythms with a global following.
bio: An ensemble blending accessible melodies, accomplished musicianship, hypnotic rhythms and an uplifting feel. Their audience spans the USA, China and Japan, with early UK radio support from Tom Robinson on BBC 6 Music.
highlights: Audiences in the USA, China and Japan

name: Wonky Logic
line: Jazz, club production and cinematic composition from Dwayne Kilvington.
bio: Dwayne Kilvington is a Leeds-born, London-based composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist. His work moves across jazz, electronic music and contemporary composition, bringing improvisation, club-influenced production and cinematic writing into one flexible identity. It grew out of collaboration in DIY and community music scenes.
highlights: Composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist
Roots in DIY and community music scenes

line: Afro, hip-hop and jazz from the emcee of K.O.G. & The Zongo Brigade.
